outcome: Uptake of complete postnatal care services
cohort: 568 women who gave birth at least 6 weeks prior to the study in the Ezha district of southern Ethiopia
finding: The uptake of complete postnatal care services was low, and factors associated with higher uptake included secondary or higher maternal education, four or more antenatal care visits, cesarean delivery, good knowledge of postnatal care, and being a model household.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was a significant factor associated with increased uptake of complete postnatal care services.
